newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh repeals law shielding Mujib's killers.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh repeals law shielding Mujib's killers.

text.p: Bangladesh parliament has repealed a 1975 ordinance blocking trial of the killers of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, independence leader and father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Parliament adopted the Indemnity Ordinance Repeal Bill late on Tuesday in the absence of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), which has boycotted the proceedings.
The bill, placed before parliament on Sunday, was scrutinised by a special law committee before being passed by a voice vote. Hasina's Awami league has a majority in the 330-member parliament.

"Now that the infamous ordinance has been repealed...there will be no obstruction to putting the killers of the father of the nation (Mujib) and others of his family and party on trial," State Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Abul Matin Khasru, said.
Hasina, who won general elections in June, wiped away tears as Khasru made a lengthy statement to legislators, the state-run television showed in a recorded replay of the proceedings.
Mujib, the man who led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan in 1971, was gunned down with most of his family on August 15, 1975, in the country's first military coup.
His successors promulgated the ordinance in September that year to protect Mujib's killers.
Khasru said the ordinance was "repugnant to fundamental rights and rule of law as enshrined in the constitution."
